Symptoms: Diarrhea started 3 days ago, very loose and watery
At least 4 bowel movements today, cannot count exact number
Serious fever sensation (feeling 'literally boiling'), no measured temperature
Vomiting everything including liquids, last vomit about 2 hours ago
Intermittent abdominal pain localized around the navel, tender on palpation
Pain associated with urge to defecate; comes and goes
No blood in stool or urine
Normal urination frequency and apparently normal color, last urine about 1 hour ago
No prior episodes of diarrhea; normal bowel habits once daily
Brother has had similar symptoms; reportedly an outbreak at school
Unable to keep down fluids well despite oral rehydration salts intake
step1_summary.Past medical history: None significant except occasional menstrual cramps
step1_summary.Medications/allergies: Daily vitamin D; occasional ibuprofen for menstrual cramps; no known allergies
step1_summary.Family/social history: Lives with brother and mother; brother recently had similar illness; no smoking; occasional alcohol
step1_summary.Vital signs/exam findings: No measured vitals, but patient reports high fever sensation; abdominal tenderness around navel; patient alert and able to respond
step1_summary.Labs/imaging: No labs/imaging done; recommendation for stool sample and hydration assessment

V: Mesenteric ischemia: Unlikely but could cause abdominal pain and diarrhea; however, acute severe pain and high risk factors absent
Intestinal vascular compromise: Does not fit well with transient diarrhea and low-risk patient
I: Viral gastroenteritis: Common cause of infectious diarrhea with vomiting and fever; supported by family contact and school outbreak
Bacterial gastroenteritis (e.g., Salmonella, Campylobacter): Possible bacterial cause given severity and persistent vomiting
Parasitic infection: Less likely without travel history and more chronic symptoms
N: Gastrointestinal neoplasm: Unlikely due to acute onset and patient age without warning signs
D: Dehydration secondary to vomiting and diarrhea: Highly relevant; risk of worsening
Nutritional deficiency unlikely to cause acute symptoms
I2: Medication-induced diarrhea/vomiting: Unlikely as only vitamins and occasional ibuprofen
Toxin ingestion: Possible but no history suggests this
C: Congenital malformations causing diarrhea: Unlikely at adult age with no prior symptoms
A: Autoimmune enteritis: Unlikely with acute presentation and supporting history
Allergic reaction: No rash or typical allergy signs
T: Abdominal trauma: No history of trauma
E: Endocrine/metabolic: Hyperthyroidism can cause diarrhea but no supporting signs
Diabetic ketoacidosis: No history of diabetes or other symptoms
